binders: Universally quantify pressure p and velocity u, each an arbitrary function R → R → R, with the first argument the spatial variable and the second the time variable.
Universally quantify real constants K = bulkModulus and rho = density and a real evaluation point (x,t).
For each choice of these data, assume rho ≠ 0 and the scalar derivative-and-equation predicate.
The scalar predicate existentially quantifies real numbers pt, px, ut, ux, in that order, for the selected functions, coefficients, and point.

The conclusion existentially quantifies vectors a and b in Fin 2 → R, in that order, for the same selected data under the hypotheses; it does not require uniform witnesses across different choices of data.
hypotheses: There exist pt, px, ut, ux ∈ R such that all six of the following hold simultaneously: τ ↦ p(x,τ) has derivative pt at t; ξ ↦ p(ξ,t) has derivative px at x; τ ↦ u(x,τ) has derivative ut at t; ξ ↦ u(ξ,t) has derivative ux at x; pt + K ux = 0; ut + rho⁻¹ px = 0.
conclusions: For q(ξ,τ) = (p(ξ,τ),u(ξ,τ)) and F(v₀,v₁) = (K v₁,rho⁻¹ v₀), there exist a,b ∈ R² such that τ ↦ q(x,τ) has derivative a at t, ξ ↦ F(q(ξ,t)) has derivative b at x, and a + b = (0,0), all simultaneously.
In coordinates, the asserted derivatives are those of τ ↦ (p(x,τ),u(x,τ)) and ξ ↦ (K u(ξ,t),rho⁻¹ p(ξ,t)); their sums vanish in each of the two coordinates.
mathematical_definitions: Identify Fin 2 → R with R² by listing coordinates in order 0,1; addition, zero, and real scalar multiplication are pointwise, and the topology is the product topology.
The state is q(ξ,τ)₀ = p(ξ,τ) and q(ξ,τ)₁ = u(ξ,τ).
The constant coefficient matrix is A₀₀ = 0, A₀₁ = K, A₁₀ = rho⁻¹, A₁₁ = 0.
The flux is F(v) = Av, where (Av)ᵢ = Σⱼ∈{0,1} Aᵢⱼvⱼ; thus F(q(ξ,t)) = (K u(ξ,t),rho⁻¹ p(ξ,t)).
HasDerivAt is an actual derivative-existence assertion for a one-real-variable function at a point, with a specified real or vector derivative value.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every pair of real-valued functions p and u of two real variables, every pair of real constants K and rho, and every real point (x,t), suppose rho is nonzero and the four separate space and time derivatives of p and u exist at that point. Suppose their values satisfy p_t + K u_x = 0 and u_t + rho⁻¹ p_x = 0 there. Then the two-component state q = (p,u), with flux F(q) = Aq for A = [[0,K],[rho⁻¹,0]], satisfies the pointwise vector conservation equation: the time derivative of τ ↦ q(x,τ) and the space derivative of ξ ↦ F(q(ξ,t)) both exist, and their sum is the zero vector.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The conclusion is conditional and pointwise at the chosen (x,t). It does not assert that the scalar hypotheses or vector equation hold at every point for a fixed pair of functions.
Both functions are defined on all of R × R, and the derivatives are ordinary derivatives on full real-variable slices, not one-sided or within-set derivatives.
K and rho are fixed real coefficients in the differentiation operations. Spatially or temporally varying coefficients are not represented.
Density is required to be nonzero but need not be positive. Bulk modulus has no sign or nonzero restriction, so K = 0 and negative K are allowed.
All four scalar partial derivatives must exist at the selected point. No joint differentiability, continuous differentiability, or derivative existence at other points is assumed.
The matrix has exactly two rows and two columns, and the state has exactly two components; there is no empty-index vacuity in the instantiated conclusion.

If density is zero, or the scalar derivative-and-equation hypothesis fails, the implication imposes no conclusion for that choice of data. The hypotheses are nevertheless satisfiable, for example by constant p and u with nonzero density.

The existential derivative witnesses in the hypothesis and conclusion are separately scoped. The conclusion does not explicitly prescribe a = (pt,ut) and b = (K ux,rho⁻¹ px), although these values follow from the derivative assertions.

The proposition asserts only the forward implication. It does not state a converse, existence or uniqueness of solutions, initial or boundary conditions, integral conservation, weak-solution semantics, or hyperbolicity.
The labels pressure, velocity, bulk modulus, and density impose no additional physical interpretation, units, or admissibility conditions beyond the displayed real types and hypotheses.
